scope: The sign of the canonical signed-decimal comparator used for static sequence bounds and position checks.
claim: For canonical unsigned digit lists and coherent signs, the PHP width/ASCII-lexicographic comparison induces exactly the mathematical strict signed integer order. The direct constructor admits a subset of these canonical forms.
assumptions: The checked signed decimal operand is the canonical ASCII PHP spelling of the Lean magnitude and sign.
Same-sign operands have equal sign-prefix width. PHP strlen reports byte length and strcmp orders equal-length ASCII digit strings lexicographically.
An operand whose sign is negative has nonzero magnitude. The proof covers all canonical widths. The pinned PHP constructor limits those widths to the native signed 64-bit domain.
limits: The proof covers the comparison rule. Native sequence generation, storage width selection, type-change transitions and rendered SQL have separate obligations.

body: Check::input(strlen($magnitude) < 19 || strcmp($magnitude, $maximum) <= 0, 'Integer is outside the signed 64-bit range.');

axioms.propext: Lean core integer comparison lemmas use propositional extensionality.
